content:
An airport pickup at Dubai International works like this: you book a chauffeur before you fly, your flight is tracked from the moment it takes off, and when you walk out of customs your driver is standing in the arrivals hall holding a board with your name on it. You do not queue, you do not phone anyone, and you do not haggle. With a private chauffeur pickup at DXB from Emirates Limo, the price is fixed when you book and the first 60 minutes of waiting are free.

How do airport pickups work at Dubai International (DXB)?

You book online with your flight number, and the chauffeur is assigned to that flight rather than to a clock time. When the aircraft lands, the 60 minutes of free waiting time starts, so you can clear passport control and collect bags at your own pace. Your driver waits inside the arrivals hall of your terminal with a name board, takes your luggage and walks you to the car parked in the airport car park.

That is the whole process from the passenger's side. The rest of this guide covers which terminal you will land at, exactly where to look for the driver, what happens when a flight is delayed, and the handful of things that go wrong when people get it wrong.

What are the key facts about a DXB pickup at a glance?

What do you need to have ready for a DXB pickup?

Five details make a pickup run without a single message being exchanged. Have them to hand when you book, not when you land.

  • Your flight number (for example EK 002), not just the airline and the time
  • The scheduled arrival date in Dubai local time, which matters for overnight flights that land the next day
  • The full address of your hotel, apartment or office, including the building name
  • Passenger and luggage counts, so the right vehicle is assigned
  • A mobile number that works on arrival, even if only on the airport Wi-Fi
  • Any child seat request, which Emirates Limo fits on request when you book

Which terminal will you arrive at in Dubai?

Your airline decides your terminal, and your booking confirmation will state it. DXB has three terminals, and according to Dubai Airports Terminal 3 and its A, B and C concourses are primarily used by Emirates, flydubai, United and Air Canada, while Terminal 1's D Gates serve numerous other international carriers and Terminal 2 handles regional and international flights from its F Gates.

If you are flying Emirates there is no ambiguity. The airline confirms on its Dubai International page that every Emirates flight arrives at and departs from gates A, B or C at Terminal 3.

Emirates Limo reads the terminal from your flight number, so you do not need to work this out yourself. It still helps to know, because Terminal 2 sits on the opposite side of the airfield from Terminals 1 and 3, and a passenger who walks out of the wrong building will not find a driver waiting.

Where exactly does the chauffeur meet you at DXB?

Inside the arrivals hall, after customs, holding a board with your name on it. You will pass passport control, collect your bags from the belt, walk through the customs channel, and step out into the public arrivals area where people are waiting behind the barriers. Your chauffeur is among them, in smart dress, with your name printed clearly.

There is no kerbside meeting point to look for. Dubai Airports states plainly that there is no pick-up area at arrivals and that anyone collecting a passenger should use the car park facility available at all terminals. This is why a name board pickup is the only method that has you met at the door rather than told to walk somewhere.

Once you have found each other, the chauffeur takes your luggage and walks you to the car in the short-stay car park. The walk is a few minutes, on the flat, with the driver pushing the trolley. If you are travelling with someone who needs assistance, mention it at booking and the driver will meet you as close to the exit as the airport allows.

What happens if your flight is early, late or diverted?

Nothing changes for you, and nothing is charged. Emirates Limo tracks your flight and moves the pickup time automatically, so a driver booked for a 14:00 landing will be in the hall at 15:30 if the aircraft lands at 15:30. Your 60 minutes of free waiting starts when the wheels touch down, not at the scheduled time.

Early arrivals are handled the same way. Tailwinds regularly bring long-haul flights into DXB ahead of schedule, and because the driver follows the flight rather than the booking time, they are in position before you reach the hall.

You can check the live status of any arrival yourself on the Dubai Airports flight information page. If your airline cancels or reroutes you onto a different flight, send the new flight number by WhatsApp to +971 56 996 4924 and the booking is moved across. A changed flight number is the one thing tracking cannot catch on its own.

How long does it take to get from DXB into Dubai?

Around 20 minutes to Downtown and the DIFC, around 30 minutes to Jumeirah and Business Bay, and around 40 to 50 minutes to Dubai Marina, JBR and the Palm, outside the busiest hours. The airport sits close to the old city on the Deira side, so anything along Sheikh Zayed Road is a straight run once you are out of the airport tunnels.

The times above are typical daytime figures and not a promise. Weekday mornings between about 7 and 9 and the evening run between about 5 and 8 add time on Sheikh Zayed Road, and Friday afternoons around the malls are slow. Your chauffeur checks live traffic before setting off and picks the route that is moving.

Many routes out of the airport pass a Salik toll gate, which is charged electronically as the car drives under it. The chauffeur's price is fixed at booking, so you will not be asked for cash in the car and there is nothing to register.

One thing worth knowing if you booked flights into the wrong airport: DXB and Al Maktoum International (DWC) are about 60 km apart on opposite sides of the city, as Dubai Airports notes in its transfer guidance. Emirates Limo covers both, so a Dubai airport transfer booking works for a DWC landing exactly as it does for DXB.

What goes wrong with airport pickups, and how do you avoid it?

Almost every failed pickup comes down to one of five causes, and every one is avoidable. Here is the list, in the order we see them.

The wrong flight number

A codeshare booking shows one flight number on your ticket and another on the aircraft. Give the operating carrier's number, the one on the departure board, and tracking will follow the right aircraft.

Walking out at the wrong terminal

Terminals 1 and 3 are connected, and it is possible to leave through the wrong hall after a long walk from the gate. Follow the signs for Arrivals and Exit in your own terminal and do not follow other passengers heading to the metro or the connections desk.

Leaving the hall to find the car

Some passengers see the doors, step outside and start looking for a black car at the kerb. There is no kerbside pickup at DXB, so the driver is behind you in the hall. Stay inside the arrivals area until you have found the name board.

A phone that does not work on landing

A driver who cannot reach you cannot tell you where they are standing. Connect to the free airport Wi-Fi before you leave the belt, or buy a local SIM at the kiosks in the arrivals hall, and keep WhatsApp open.

Late changes that never reach the driver

A hotel change, an extra passenger or a rebooked flight all need to be sent to +971 56 996 4924 as soon as you know. A last-minute change told to the driver at the car can still be handled, but a message an hour earlier means the right vehicle is already waiting.

Cancellations follow one rule with no exceptions. Cancel 24 hours or more before the pickup time and you get a full refund; cancel inside 24 hours, or fail to show, and the booking is charged in full.

Should you book a chauffeur, take a taxi or use the metro from DXB?

A chauffeur is the right choice when you are arriving with luggage, a family, a colleague you want to impress, or after a long-haul night flight. The metro is the right choice for a solo traveller with a backpack heading somewhere on the Red Line in daylight. A taxi sits in between and depends on the queue you find.

OptionWhere you find itWhat to expectBest for
Private chauffeur (Emirates Limo)Name board inside the arrivals hallFixed price set at booking, flight tracked, 60 minutes free waiting, luggage carriedFamilies, business travellers, night arrivals, anyone with bags
TaxiDesignated ranks at each terminal, 24/7, per Dubai AirportsMetered, queue length varies with the arrivals bankSolo or pair travel, light luggage, no fixed budget
Dubai Metro Red LineStations at Terminals 1 and 3, per Dubai AirportsRuns from 5AM most days, closes around midnight, Nol card needed, no Terminal 2 stationBackpackers, daytime arrivals, destinations near a Red Line station

Two practical notes on the public options. The metro does not run all night, with Dubai Airports listing a 5AM start on most days and an 8AM start on Sundays, so a 2AM landing rules it out. And the metro has no station at Terminal 2, so passengers landing there need a road transfer regardless.

If you are staying somewhere central and want the car to carry on after check-in, an hourly chauffeur from AED 150 per hour keeps the driver with you for as many stops as you like.

How do you book a DXB pickup with Emirates Limo?

Booking takes a couple of minutes on the Dubai airport transfer page. Choose the airport as your pickup, enter the destination address, date and time, and the form shows you the fixed price for each vehicle before you commit.

Pick your car from the fleet: a Lexus ES300 or Mercedes-Benz S-Class for up to three or four passengers, a GMC Yukon or Mercedes-Benz V-Class for a family of six with six bags, or a Kia Carnival for five. Then add your flight number, passenger details and any child seat request.

Pay by card online and the confirmation lands in your inbox straight away. Heading to a hotel rather than a private address? The airport to hotel transfer page is the same product with the hotel search built in, and the driver will already know the right entrance.

Emirates Limo runs 24 hours a day, every day of the year, including public holidays, so a 3AM landing is met the same way as a 3PM one. Questions on waiting time, cancellation or child seats are answered on the FAQ page, or on WhatsApp at +971 56 996 4924.

faqs.question: Where does my driver meet me at Dubai International Airport?
faqs.answer: Inside the arrivals hall of your terminal, after customs, holding a board with your name on it. Dubai Airports has no kerbside pick-up area at arrivals, so your Emirates Limo chauffeur waits with the other greeters behind the barriers, takes your luggage and walks you to the car in the airport car park.

faqs.question: What happens if my flight to DXB is delayed?
faqs.answer: Nothing changes and nothing is charged. Emirates Limo tracks your flight and moves the pickup automatically to the actual landing time. Your 60 minutes of free waiting starts when the aircraft lands, not at the scheduled time, so a two-hour delay costs you nothing extra.

faqs.question: Which terminal do Emirates flights arrive at in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Terminal 3. Emirates confirms that every one of its flights arrives at and departs from gates A, B or C at Terminal 3 at Dubai International. flydubai, United and Air Canada also use Terminal 3, while Terminal 1 and Terminal 2 serve other international and regional carriers.

faqs.question: How much free waiting time do I get on an airport pickup?
faqs.answer: 60 minutes at any airport, counted from the actual landing time rather than the scheduled one. That covers passport control, baggage collection and customs for nearly every arrival. For pickups anywhere other than an airport, the free waiting time is 15 minutes.

faqs.question: Can I cancel a DXB airport pickup for free?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you cancel 24 hours or more before the pickup time you receive a full refund. Cancellations inside 24 hours of the pickup time, and no-shows, are charged in full. There is no other tier, so if plans might change, cancel early and rebook once you know.
